column1: {"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "cart-service", "root cause reason": "The failure mechanism is 'connection pool exhausted' in cart-service. Both the error_log and OpenTelemetry trace confirm that at 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC, cart-service hit a DatabaseTimeoutError because all 10 connections in the pool were active with 0 idle \u2014 meaning the service could no longer acquire a DB connection. Frontend has zero anomalous events of its own and is almost certainly surfacing errors as a downstream consumer of cart-service (e.g. add-to-cart or checkout calls failing and propagating HTTP 500s upstream to frontend). The causal chain is: DB connection pool saturation \u2192 cart-service errors \u2192 frontend failures. Cart-service is Patient Zero."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "payment-service", "root cause reason": "OOM crash (Java heap space exhaustion with GC overhead limit exceeded) is the explicit failure mechanism. payment-service has two corroborating signals \u2014 an error_log and an OpenTelemetry trace log \u2014 both timestamped 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC, making it the earliest anomalous event in the incident timeline. api-gateway has zero logged events of its own, indicating its error status is symptomatic: it is alerting because downstream calls to payment-service are failing (timeouts or connection refused) after the OOM crash rendered payment-service unable to process requests. The causal chain is: payment-service JVM heap exhausted \u2192 GC overhead limit exceeded \u2192 service unresponsive \u2192 api-gateway upstream calls fail \u2192 api-gateway enters error state."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "notification-service", "root cause reason": "The failure mechanism is an 'invalid or expired API key' (AuthenticationError: 401 Unauthorized). notification-service is the only service with concrete anomalous events, both error_log and OTEL traces converging on the same timestamp (2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC). order-service shows error status but has zero associated events, indicating it is symptomatic \u2014 likely failing because it cannot complete workflows that depend on notification-service (e.g., order confirmation or alert dispatch). The 401 error is self-contained to notification-service's outbound authentication, meaning an API key rotation, expiration, or misconfiguration occurred there first, cascading degraded status upstream to order-service."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "auth-service", "root cause reason": "The only anomalous events with concrete timestamps originate in auth-service at 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC. The failure mechanism is a missing database index on users.session_token causing a slow query (7842ms) \u2014 a classic 'full table scan on session lookup' scenario. Auth-service is a synchronous upstream dependency for both frontend and checkout-service: when session validation queries time out or stall, frontend login/session flows and checkout authentication gates block or return errors, propagating the outage downstream. Frontend and checkout-service show error status but carry zero independent anomalous events, confirming they are symptomatic dependents rather than causal origins. The corroborating OTEL trace and error_log both point to the same root event, increasing confidence."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "event-processor", "root cause reason": "The earliest and only concrete anomalous timestamp belongs to event-processor at 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC. The failure mechanism is a 'consumer NullPointerException' \u2014 specifically, EventDeserializer.deserialize() threw a NullPointerException that halted the event consumer entirely. This is confirmed by two corroborating signals: an error_log entry (unix epoch 1717236001) and an OTel error_log entry, both describing the same exception at the same instant. The consumer stoppage in event-processor would starve downstream services (recommendation-service, analytics-service) of event data, explaining their error states with zero logged events \u2014 they are symptomatic, not causal. The api-gateway alert is a cascading effect of the pipeline stall originating here. Confidence is not 1.0 because recommendation-service and analytics-service have no telemetry to fully rule out independent faults."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "inventory-service", "root cause reason": "The only concrete anomalous events with timestamps exist on inventory-service \u2014 a query regression causing stock_count=0 for all SKUs, first recorded at 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC (corroborated by both the error_log and OTel spans). The failure mechanism is a 'query regression returning zero stock for all SKUs', likely a bad DB query, schema migration, or data truncation. Frontend and checkout-service carry no independent error events, indicating their error status is symptomatic \u2014 they are downstream consumers of inventory data. When inventory-service returns stock_count=0 universally, checkout-service cannot complete purchases (likely 'out of stock' guard failures) and frontend surfaces errors to end users, which is the natural error propagation path: inventory-service \u2192 checkout-service \u2192 frontend. No earlier timestamp exists for any other service, confirming inventory-service is Patient Zero."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "shipping-service", "root cause reason": "The failure mechanism is a 'postal code format validation ParseError' \u2014 shipping-service is the only node with concrete anomalous events (2 matching error signals: one raw error_log and one corroborated Otel trace, both pointing to the same ParseError: invalid postal code format for locale en_GB, expected 6 alphanumeric chars). The earliest confirmed timestamp is 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC (Unix 1717236001 corroborates this). api-gateway and order-service carry zero logged events of their own, indicating their error status is symptomatic \u2014 they are surfacing failures propagated upstream from shipping-service's inability to process UK postal codes. The causal chain is: shipping-service rejects/throws on malformed postal code input \u2192 order-service receives error response or timeout \u2192 api-gateway surfaces the failure to the caller and enters error state. shipping-service is causal, not symptomatic, because it holds the only originating fault signal."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "config-service", "root cause reason": "The only timestamped anomalous events in the entire incident belong to config-service, firing at 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC. The failure mechanism is explicit: a Redis FLUSHALL was executed against the cache backing config-service, causing a total eviction of all feature-flag keys. config-service is now serving default/fallback values for every feature flag. Downstream services (payment-service, search-service, recommendation-service) have zero logged events of their own, indicating their error status is symptomatic \u2014 they are likely misbehaving because feature flags that control their runtime behavior (circuit breaker thresholds, rollout gates, killswitches, etc.) have reverted to defaults, destabilising them. api-gateway fired the alert as the outermost observer. The causal chain is: Redis FLUSHALL \u2192 config-service cache miss \u2192 incorrect/default feature flags served \u2192 downstream service failures \u2192 api-gateway alert. config-service is causal; all others are symptomatic."}

{"root cause occurrence datetime": "2024-06-01 10:00:00", "root cause component": "api-gateway", "root cause reason": "Misconfigured rate limiting is the failure mechanism. Both the error_log and otel/error_log events on api-gateway explicitly identify config key rate_limit_mode=global, meaning the gateway is enforcing a single 10 req/s ceiling across ALL users rather than per-user limits. This misconfiguration causes legitimate traffic to be blanket-throttled at the gateway edge, starving downstream services (search-service, cart-service, user-service) of requests they would otherwise handle \u2014 their error status is symptomatic of being unreachable or request-starved, not independently faulty. No anomalous events are recorded on any downstream service, confirming they are collateral victims. The earliest correlated timestamp is 2024-06-01T10:00:00 UTC. The fault is causal at api-gateway because the configuration error lives there and all downstream degradation flows from it."}
